teams.heading: Fijian forward Saimoni Vunilagi passes away in Japan after suspected heatstroke
teams.body: The Fijian rugby community is mourning back-row forward Saimoni Vunilagi, who passed away on Friday 7 August in Fukuoka after showing severe symptoms of heatstroke following a Kyushu KV training session. The 26-year-old, who stood 196cm and weighed 117kg, began his professional career in Japan in 2023. His second-division club expressed deep devastation, stating that the player's 'generous spirit and powerful style of play had raised high hopes' for his future contributions.

lead.why: The tragic death of Fijian player Saimoni Vunilagi in Japan from suspected heatstroke is the highest-salience story in the rugby press.

teams.heading: Ollie Lawrence and Elliot Daly lose England central contracts in Borthwick reshuffle
teams.body: Steve Borthwick has omitted Ollie Lawrence and Elliot Daly from England’s new 25-man central contract list, a significant move ahead of next year's World Cup. While Daly was nursing an arm injury during the Nations Championship, Lawrence’s exclusion comes as a surprise following his recent form against the All Blacks. In their place, the head coach has fast-tracked Alex Coles, Seb Atkinson and the versatile Asher Opoku-Fordjour. Borthwick now has greater control over this core group, who receive approximately £150,000 a season.

teams.heading: Tributes flow for Edmund Van Esbeck after former Irish Times correspondent dies
teams.body: The Irish rugby community is mourning the death of Edmund ‘Ned’ Van Esbeck at the age of 94. The former Irish Times correspondent spent more than 30 years documenting the national team’s evolution, covering 18 overseas tours and the sport's transition into the professional era. IRFU chief executive Kevin Potts expressed ‘sincere condolences’ yesterday, acknowledging Van Esbeck’s status as an authoritative historian and a hugely influential voice. His 34-year tenure at the newspaper remains a definitive record of the game’s modern history.

lead.why: The death of a legendary correspondent is the day's most significant and salient hard news item for the Irish rugby community.

teams.heading: Alun Wyn Jones returns to Ospreys as a new board director
teams.body: Former Wales captain Alun Wyn Jones has joined the Ospreys board of directors with immediate effect. The 40-year-old returns to the club where he made 257 appearances during a turbulent period for the region, which currently faces an uncertain future amid Welsh Rugby Union plans to reduce the professional game to three sides. Chairman James Davies-Yandle stated the club was not looking for a mere figurehead, but a director who understands the organisation from the inside to help drive long-term stability.

teams.body: The Pumas were convincingly beaten 38-14 by the Griquas in Nelspruit on Friday, a result that complicates their position on the Currie Cup log. teams.heading: Anton Segner ruled out as Simon Parker joins All Blacks bench
teams.body: Coach Dave Rennie has been forced into a late change for today’s series opener at Ellis Park, with loose forward Anton Segner withdrawing due to a swollen ankle. Medical assessments have diagnosed the issue as acute inflammatory arthritis, with the player's return to play yet to be determined. Simon Parker has been called into the match-day 23 to replace him, joining a bench that also features Peter Lakai, Fletcher Newell, George Bower, and Asafo Aumua.
